topics.title: Everyday greetings and politeness

foundationA1.outcome: Greet an unfamiliar adult, answer a check-in and close the exchange.

a2.outcome: Proposed revisit, no current A2 lesson: adapt a greeting or apology to a changed relationship.

communicativeTask.situation: Meeting a neighbour at the building entrance
communicativeTask.promptEn: Role-play a daytime meeting with a neighbour addressed as vous. Ask how they are, answer their return question and leave politely. In a second round meet a friend.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Bonjour ! Comment allez-vous ? — Très bien, merci. Et vous ? — Ça va bien, merci. Bonne journée !
communicativeTask.modelEn: Hello! How are you? — Very well, thank you. And you? — I am well, thank you. Have a good day!
successCriteria: Choose an arrival greeting and a departure wish for their different functions.
Keep vous forms together; use compatible familiar forms in the friend round.

revision.transferTaskEn: Choose an evening arrival and departure phrase for a new role card.

gaps: Shared fr.bonjour gloss omits afternoon; coordinate any support revision across all uses.
Add arrival-versus-leaving and register decisions beyond the current recognition question.

future.B1: Manage introductions and changes of register in a small group.
future.B2: Handle nuanced greetings, interruptions and relationship-sensitive closings.

topics.title: Essential conversation tools

foundationA1.outcome: Ask for repetition or written help and check one understood detail.

a2.outcome: Proposed revisit, no current A2 lesson: clarify two linked instructions and explain the unclear part.

communicativeTask.situation: A helper gives a hidden short code
communicativeTask.promptEn: Partner A sees a three-digit code. Ask for repetition or slower speech, write it and read it back. A confirms or corrects it.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Vous pouvez répéter plus lentement ? — Deux, six, huit. — Deux, six, huit, c’est bien ça ? — Oui.
communicativeTask.modelEn: Can you repeat that more slowly? — Two, six, eight. — Two, six, eight, is that right? — Yes.
successCriteria: Recover the exact code after clarification.
Read it back for confirmation rather than only claim understanding.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask a receptionist to write a fictional surname instead of a code.

gaps: Alphabet letter-name recognition needs early support; épeler alone is not an alphabet course.
Practise the repair-and-confirm loop beyond the current single sentence.

future.B1: Resolve a misunderstanding and reformulate an instruction.
future.B2: Negotiate precise meaning and tactfully challenge ambiguity.

topics.title: Numbers and quantities

clusters.title: Count people and read a code

foundationA1.outcome: Give a small quantity or code and recognise common prices with supported number-building patterns.

a2.outcome: Proposed revisit, no current A2 lesson: compare totals and check a simple payment discrepancy.

communicativeTask.situation: A counter with separate quantity and price cards
communicativeTask.promptEn: A sees the quantity order; B sees prices. Ask for the quantity and total, then read the total back. Start under twenty and repeat with a larger total.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Vous êtes combien ? — Nous sommes quatre. — Ça fait vingt euros en tout. — Vingt euros, c’est bien ça ?
communicativeTask.modelEn: How many of you are there? — There are four of us. — That is twenty euros altogether. — Twenty euros, is that right?
successCriteria: Transfer the quantity accurately.
Confirm the total in euros; arithmetic may be supported.

revision.transferTaskEn: Read a fictional reference code digit by digit and distinguish it from a price.

gaps: Zero to nineteen and tens through one hundred already have targets; do not duplicate those cards.
Add varied construction and recognition practice for 21, 31, 71, 80, 81 and 91; rules alone do not establish independent numeracy.

future.B1: Explain a simple budget and correct a misunderstood amount.
future.B2: Qualify numerical comparisons and budget trade-offs.

topics.title: People and introductions

foundationA1.outcome: Introduce yourself, say where you live and identify someone close to you.

a2.outcome: Describe arriving recently and keep a short first conversation going with repair support.

communicativeTask.situation: First meeting in a shared building
communicativeTask.promptEn: Partners have different fictional names, origins, home cities and language cards. Exchange these details, then introduce one relative or friend.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je m’appelle Alex. Je viens de Londres, mais j’habite à Nantes. Et vous ? — Moi, c’est Léa. Ma sœur habite ici.
communicativeTask.modelEn: My name is Alex. I come from London, but I live in Nantes. And you? — I am Léa. My sister lives here.
successCriteria: Exchange a name and distinguish origin from residence.
Identify a relationship with an appropriate possessive.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask how to spell an unfamiliar fictional surname.

gaps: Age, mother/father/partner and early contact-detail transfer are proposed additions.
Bridge canonical contact details from Administration into the early identity route.
First-meeting dialogue adds a second-floor ordinal before it is targeted; provide visible support.

future.B1: Describe relationships, changes of home and personal background.
future.B2: Explain complex identity and belonging with nuanced relationship vocabulary.

topics.title: Dates and availability

foundationA1.outcome: Name a weekday or month and agree a simple day.

a2.outcome: Offer an alternative calendar date and confirm availability.

communicativeTask.situation: Two different appointment calendars
communicativeTask.promptEn: Give partners different free dates. Find a shared date, reject an unavailable one and confirm day and month. The first pass may use a visible calendar.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Vous êtes disponible le premier juin ? — Non, mais je peux venir le trois juin. — D’accord, le trois juin.
communicativeTask.modelEn: Are you available on the first of June? — No, but I can come on the third of June. — All right, the third of June.
successCriteria: Find a date available to both people.
Repeat day and month, distinguishing premier from ordinary day numbers.

revision.transferTaskEn: Write the agreed date in a short fictional confirmation message.

gaps: All seven weekdays and all twelve months already appear as targets.
Practise specific lundi versus habitual le lundi in a schedule task.
Add supported year/date reading after checking number load.

future.B1: Explain scheduling constraints over several weeks.
future.B2: Negotiate conflicting schedules and qualify uncertain availability.

topics.title: Time and daily routine

foundationA1.outcome: Say when you get ready and leave, using a clock time and a simple habit.

a2.outcome: Describe an ordered day and distinguish a usual habit from an occasional change.

communicativeTask.situation: Housemates coordinate their morning
communicativeTask.promptEn: Each partner has a different start time and bathroom slot. Ask about getting up and leaving, then agree a workable morning order.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Tu te lèves à quelle heure ? — À sept heures. Ensuite, je prends mon petit déjeuner. Et toi ? — À sept heures et demie.
communicativeTask.modelEn: What time do you get up? — At seven. Then I have breakfast. And you? — At half past seven.
successCriteria: Exchange two meaningful clock times.
Give a two-step sequence and keep reflexive pronouns with their speaker.

revision.transferTaskEn: Describe a weekend change to the weekday routine.

gaps: Daily-actions is currently A2 although its supported task resembles A1; review level only with a complete revision.
Add quarter-hour and 24-hour practice; et demie alone is not full clock coverage.
Keep tard distinct from en retard and waking up distinct from getting up.

future.B1: Describe changing habits and explain a disrupted day.
future.B2: Evaluate work-life routines and competing time demands.

topics.title: Finding your way on foot

foundationA1.outcome: Ask where a service is and follow two short walking instructions.

a2.outcome: Check walking time and correct a missed turn.

communicativeTask.situation: A map with a missing destination label
communicativeTask.promptEn: A sees the library location; B has an incomplete map. Ask where it is, follow the route and mark it. In the revisit, start from the wrong side of the bridge.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Où se trouve la bibliothèque ? — Allez tout droit, puis tournez à droite au feu. — À droite au feu, c’est bien ça ?
communicativeTask.modelEn: Where is the library? — Go straight on, then turn right at the traffic light. — Right at the traffic light, is that right?
successCriteria: Identify the same destination on both maps.
Clarify a turn or landmark before marking it.

revision.transferTaskEn: Locate a post office with a different pair of landmarks.

gaps: Add map transfer to current meaning recognition.
Bridge un bureau de poste in canonical support with la poste in dialogue.

future.B1: Explain a longer route and recover from an unexpected closure.
future.B2: Compare urban access, transport design and mobility constraints.

topics.title: Transport

foundationA1.outcome: Ask for a destination, identify a stop and buy a one-way or return ticket.

a2.outcome: Check a connection or ask for an alternative after a cancellation.

communicativeTask.situation: A ticket desk with different timetable cards
communicativeTask.promptEn: A has a destination and arrival deadline; B has two fictional services. Choose a service and ticket. In A2, B cancels the first choice and offers a replacement.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Mon train est annulé. Il y a un autre itinéraire ? — Vous pouvez prendre le car de remplacement. — Il part d’où ?
communicativeTask.modelEn: My train is cancelled. Is there another route? — You can take the replacement coach. — Where does it leave from?
successCriteria: Confirm the destination and a relevant service time in the first round.
Obtain an alternative and its departure point in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask which platform serves a changed connection.

gaps: Keep ticket-validation arrangements fictional or phrased as questions.
Separate transport service times from working hours.
Routine alternative requests do not amount to a formal compensation complaint.

future.B1: Explain a missed connection and negotiate a travel solution.
future.B2: Evaluate disruption policies and sustainable mobility options.

topics.title: Bakery

foundationA1.outcome: Order bread or pastries with a quantity and close the purchase politely.

a2.outcome: Ask for a takeaway adjustment or arrange an order and collection time.

communicativeTask.situation: A bakery order and availability card
communicativeTask.promptEn: Customer has a quantity and collection preference; baker has stock and two collection slots. Complete a basic purchase, then agree a later collection.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je voudrais commander un gâteau pour samedi. — Pour combien de personnes ? — Pour six. Je peux venir le chercher à dix heures ?
communicativeTask.modelEn: I would like to order a cake for Saturday. — For how many people? — For six. Can I come and collect it at ten?
successCriteria: Identify an available item and quantity in the basic round.
Agree day, collection time and number of people in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Request sliced bread when the first choice is unavailable.

gaps: fr.bakery.buy-lunch has corrupted grammar question punctuation; a separate draft correction is supplied.
Shared polite examples mention coffee; use local dialogue for bakery transfer.
Regional pastry names are an extension, not a replacement canonical target.

future.B1: Clarify a custom order and resolve a collection misunderstanding.
future.B2: Negotiate detailed event catering requirements and trade-offs.

topics.title: Groceries

foundationA1.outcome: Buy a small food list and ask for a quantity or price.

a2.outcome: Locate a product section and check a price discrepancy politely.

communicativeTask.situation: A shopping list and mismatching receipt
communicativeTask.promptEn: Shopper has a list; assistant has section locations. Find the items, then compare a fictional shelf label with a receipt containing one mismatch.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Excusez-moi, il y a une erreur sur le prix. — Quel prix avez-vous vu ? — Deux euros sur l’étiquette.
communicativeTask.modelEn: Excuse me, there is a mistake in the price. — What price did you see? — Two euros on the label.
successCriteria: Obtain the requested product and quantity in the basic round.
Identify the mismatching amount and ask for checking in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Repeat the checking exchange with a new product and amount.

gaps: fr.groceries.find-products has corrupted question punctuation; a separate correction is drafted.
Finding a section is A1-like supported performance despite its current A2 label; review separately.
A price-check request does not establish successful recovery of money.

future.B1: Explain a purchase problem and negotiate an available remedy.
future.B2: Compare food costs, sourcing and consumption choices with qualified reasons.

topics.title: Restaurant

foundationA1.outcome: Request a table, choose a drink or meal and ask for the bill.

a2.outcome: State a food need, request information and ask about separate payment.

communicativeTask.situation: An original menu and a diner request card
communicativeTask.promptEn: Server sees a short original menu; customer has a preference and party size. Agree an order. In A2 add an allergy card: server checks information instead of guessing.
communicativeTask.modelFr: J’ai une allergie aux œufs. Cette sauce contient des œufs ? — Je vais vérifier en cuisine. — Merci, je vais attendre.
communicativeTask.modelEn: I have an allergy to eggs. Does this sauce contain eggs? — I will check with the kitchen. — Thank you, I will wait.
successCriteria: Agree party size and ordered item in the basic round.
State the allergy explicitly and request ingredient information; task completion is not a safety guarantee.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask about separate payment and request a receipt after a new meal.

gaps: fr.restaurant.finish-the-meal has corrupted grammar punctuation; separate correction drafted.
Preserve la carte versus un menu and receipt versus transport-ticket senses.
Keep allergy and sauce-on-the-side requests distinct.

future.B1: Explain an order problem and request an appropriate resolution.
future.B2: Discuss food-service choices and competing dietary requirements.

topics.title: Clothes and shopping

foundationA1.outcome: Find a garment and ask for another size or colour.

a2.outcome: Explain a fit problem or defect and ask whether an exchange is possible.

communicativeTask.situation: A clothing request and a stock card
communicativeTask.promptEn: Customer needs a size and colour; assistant sees available options. Find an acceptable garment. In A2 use a defect card and proof of purchase to request an exchange.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je voudrais rapporter ce pull. Il y a un défaut. — Vous avez le ticket de caisse ? — Oui. Un échange est possible ?
communicativeTask.modelEn: I would like to bring this jumper back. There is a defect. — Do you have the till receipt? — Yes. Is an exchange possible?
successCriteria: Agree an available garment, size and colour.
Identify a defect and ask for a remedy without assuming entitlement.

revision.transferTaskEn: Change from clothing size to shoe size, using pointure.

gaps: Only blue and black are explicit basic colour targets; a bounded broader cluster is proposed.
Canonical chercher example is food-shop specific; local dialogue supplies clothes context.
Supported routine exchange enquiries differ from extended formal complaints.

future.B1: Explain a purchase history and negotiate a remedy.
future.B2: Make a sustained tactful complaint and weigh policy terms.

topics.title: Home and housing

foundationA1.outcome: Describe a home and understand how to reach or enter it.

a2.outcome: Ask what rent includes or report a fault and agree a visit.

communicativeTask.situation: Two floor plans and a repair diary
communicativeTask.promptEn: Describe rooms so a partner completes missing labels. In the revisit, tenant has a fault and availability card; contact has two visit slots. Agree a visit and repeat the fault.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Le chauffage ne fonctionne pas depuis hier. Vous pouvez faire venir quelqu’un ? — Demain matin ? — Oui, je serai là.
communicativeTask.modelEn: The heating has not worked since yesterday. Can you arrange for someone to come? — Tomorrow morning? — Yes, I will be there.
successCriteria: Place two rooms or objects correctly in the basic round.
Give the fault, starting time and agreed visit slot in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Report another fault with the same request frame.

gaps: fr.housing.ask-about-a-rental has corrupted question punctuation; separate correction drafted.
Research viewing, deposit and guarantor language before adding targets.
Rent example uses eight hundred before explicit hundreds-building practice; provide numerical support.

future.B1: Explain rental constraints and follow up an unresolved repair.
future.B2: Negotiate complex housing needs and evaluate housing-policy trade-offs.

topics.title: Leisure and weather

foundationA1.outcome: Say what you like and agree an activity using the weather.

a2.outcome: Suggest a weather-dependent alternative and postpone an outing.

communicativeTask.situation: Activity preferences and different forecasts
communicativeTask.promptEn: Partners have different preferences and one forecast each. Find an activity both accept; in A2 agree a backup if it rains.
communicativeTask.modelFr: S’il pleut, on va au musée ? — Oui. On reporte la promenade à dimanche ? — D’accord.
communicativeTask.modelEn: If it rains, shall we go to the museum? — Yes. Shall we postpone the walk until Sunday? — All right.
successCriteria: Choose one shared activity and time.
Make the condition and alternative explicit in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Invite a friend to a different indoor activity after a forecast change.

gaps: Weather is already present; seasons and snow remain proposed target gaps.
Recycled invitations belong here for a weather decision and in Social for arrangements.
Teach si in a short present-tense chunk before broader conditional grammar.

future.B1: Explain leisure habits and a changed plan with reasons.
future.B2: Discuss access to leisure, cultural preferences and environmental constraints.

topics.title: Invitations and shared plans

foundationA1.outcome: Invite someone, accept or decline warmly and suggest another occasion.

a2.outcome: Agree place and time, change a plan and confirm new details.

communicativeTask.situation: Friends with conflicting availability cards
communicativeTask.promptEn: Each partner sees only their own free times. Invite, decline an unsuitable time, offer an alternative and confirm where and when.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Tu veux venir chez moi samedi ? — Désolée, je ne peux pas. Dimanche plutôt ? — Oui, à huit heures ? — Ça me va.
communicativeTask.modelEn: Do you want to come to my place on Saturday? — Sorry, I cannot. Sunday instead? — Yes, at eight? — That works for me.
successCriteria: Respond to the actual invitation rather than recite a fixed acceptance.
Reach a shared day, time and place and repeat the changed detail.

revision.transferTaskEn: Write a two-line fictional message changing the meeting place.

gaps: Repeated Leisure invitation IDs are intentional recycling.
Provide a visible en retard gloss in organise before its later canonical bank.
Keep plan acceptance ça me va distinct from clothing fit.

future.B1: Maintain relationships while explaining and renegotiating a change.
future.B2: Handle tactful disagreement and nuanced social expectations.

topics.title: Health and appointments

foundationA1.outcome: Ask for an appointment, state where something hurts and request explanation at a pharmacy.

a2.outcome: Describe symptom timing or change an appointment and confirm the new slot.

communicativeTask.situation: A fictional appointment diary and patient card
communicativeTask.promptEn: Patient sees a simple symptom and free-time card; receptionist sees the diary. Agree an appointment. In A2 add a conflict and negotiate a new slot. Use invented health details.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je voudrais déplacer mon rendez-vous. Vous avez un créneau vendredi ? — À dix heures. — Merci, je confirme vendredi à dix heures.
communicativeTask.modelEn: I would like to reschedule my appointment. Do you have a slot on Friday? — At ten. — Thank you, I confirm Friday at ten.
successCriteria: Communicate the intended appointment day and time.
Identify the conflict and confirm the new slot; symptom language stays descriptive.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask a pharmacist to repeat and explain a fictional leaflet phrase.

gaps: Expand body parts with supported avoir mal à/au/aux; current examples already teach some contractions.
No dosage or emergency-service completeness is claimed.
Keep ongoing depuis separate from completed pendant duration.

future.B1: Explain a longer symptom history and ask follow-up questions.
future.B2: Discuss health information and public-health choices with qualified claims.

topics.title: Cooking

foundationA1.outcome: Ask for utensils, prepare vegetables and follow a short supported recipe.

a2.outcome: Explain an ordered cooking step, duration or request to put food away.

communicativeTask.situation: Housemates split an original recipe card
communicativeTask.promptEn: A sees ingredients and quantities; B sees preparation steps. Ask for missing information and agree who does two actions. This is a language practice card, not a tested recipe.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Tu peux laver les courgettes ? — Oui. Et l’oignon ? — Je le coupe. Ensuite, on ajoute un peu de sel.
communicativeTask.modelEn: Can you wash the courgettes? — Yes. And the onion? — I will cut it. Then we add a little salt.
successCriteria: Transfer an ingredient and amount.
Agree two actions in order with an appropriate request form.

revision.transferTaskEn: Use another vegetable with the same quantity and sequence language.

gaps: Explain which familiar or polite partner gives an imperative.
Cooling/storage language examples are not complete food-safety instructions.
Create an original ordered card to supplement the single sentence activity.

future.B1: Explain a recipe variation and solve a preparation problem.
future.B2: Compare food traditions and justify detailed menu choices.

topics.title: Phone and digital communication

foundationA1.outcome: Arrange a call, dictate a fictional email address and confirm a message.

a2.outcome: Explain a connection or file problem and request another way to receive a document.

communicativeTask.situation: An inaccessible attachment and fictional contact card
communicativeTask.promptEn: A cannot open an attachment; B can offer a link. Explain the problem, request a link and confirm the next action. Basic round dictates an address with one character correction.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je ne peux pas ouvrir la pièce jointe. Vous pouvez m’envoyer le lien ? — Oui. — Merci, je vais télécharger le document.
communicativeTask.modelEn: I cannot open the attachment. Can you send me the link? — Yes. — Thank you, I will download the document.
successCriteria: Transfer the fictional address accurately after a check.
Identify the inaccessible file and agree an alternative in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Leave a short fictional voicemail giving a callback time.

gaps: Bridge contact expressions into early identity work without duplicate IDs.
Use a reserved example domain in a later revision: exemple.fr is labelled fictional but is not a reserved example domain.
Practice never requires a real password.

future.B1: Explain a technical problem and compare workarounds.
future.B2: Discuss digital access, privacy and service-design trade-offs.

topics.title: Accommodation

foundationA1.outcome: Book a simple stay, give the booking name and ask about an included service.

a2.outcome: Describe a room problem or arrange luggage storage before departure.

communicativeTask.situation: A booking request and hotel availability card
communicativeTask.promptEn: Guest has dates and room needs; receptionist has two offers. Agree a booking. In A2 add a room-problem card and confirm the offered solution.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Il n’y a pas d’eau chaude dans ma chambre. Est-ce que je peux changer de chambre ? — Oui, une autre chambre est disponible. — Merci.
communicativeTask.modelEn: There is no hot water in my room. Can I change rooms? — Yes, another room is available. — Thank you.
successCriteria: Agree room type, arrival day and number of nights.
Name a problem and confirm an offered practical action in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask about checkout and leaving bags until a different time.

gaps: Retain the note that chambre double does not guarantee a bed arrangement.
Identity-document exchanges are fictional, not universal requirements.
Contrast à midi with jusqu’à midi in a timed luggage task.

future.B1: Explain a booking discrepancy and negotiate a suitable room.
future.B2: Handle detailed accommodation complaints and compare contractual options.

topics.title: Education and learning

foundationA1.outcome: Ask to join a course and check a simple classroom instruction.

a2.outcome: Report an absence, describe a difficulty and agree a practical learning goal.

communicativeTask.situation: Course timetables and learner availability
communicativeTask.promptEn: Learner has a preferred format and free times; adviser has two courses. Choose a course. In A2 tell the teacher about an absence or difficulty and request a next step.
communicativeTask.modelFr: J’ai du mal à comprendre les nombres au téléphone. — On peut refaire un petit dialogue. — Oui, à mon rythme, s’il vous plaît.
communicativeTask.modelEn: I find it difficult to understand numbers on the phone. — We can do a short dialogue again. — Yes, at my own pace, please.
successCriteria: Identify a suitable format and schedule.
State a specific difficulty and agree a practice action in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask which exercise and page to prepare after an absence.

gaps: Core classroom nouns currently live in Work.study; bridge them here using canonical recycling.
Keep avoir du mal à for difficulty distinct from physical pain.
Course labels and lesson completion are not proof of proficiency.

future.B1: Describe training experience and plan learning priorities.
future.B2: Evaluate teaching approaches and argue for a training proposal.

topics.title: Work and study

clusters.title: Find people and do a task

foundationA1.outcome: Locate a colleague or room and request help with a simple task.

a2.outcome: Clarify an instruction, check a deadline and suggest a next action.

communicativeTask.situation: A task card with an omitted deadline
communicativeTask.promptEn: Worker has a document task; colleague has the missing deadline and checking rule. Ask for both, repeat the instruction and propose a workable next action.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Il faut vérifier les noms et les numéros ? — Oui, avant midi. — D’accord. Je propose de vérifier le document ensemble.
communicativeTask.modelEn: Do we need to check the names and the numbers? — Yes, before noon. — All right. I suggest checking the document together.
successCriteria: Request needed help or a room clearly in the basic round.
Confirm task and time constraint before proposing action in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Clarify a changed work schedule instead of a document task.

gaps: fr.work.organise-work explanation refers to la absent from its dialogue; separate correction drafted.
Workplace training reuses Education concepts; it is not an unrelated new word count.
Resolve the earlier noon deadline explicitly when the dialogue also mentions a two-o’clock meeting.

future.B1: Explain a task delay and negotiate priorities.
future.B2: Present and defend a workplace proposal with nuanced trade-offs.

topics.title: Services and paperwork

foundationA1.outcome: Ask at reception, give fictional contact details and send a letter.

a2.outcome: Check a missing document and clarify a submission route or final date.

communicativeTask.situation: An original mock form and document checklist
communicativeTask.promptEn: Applicant has a partly completed fictional form; clerk has a checklist and submission date. Ask what is missing and where or when to submit it. No real eligibility decision is simulated.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Mon dossier est complet ? — Il manque votre signature sur cette page. — Je signe ici ? Et quelle est la date limite ?
communicativeTask.modelEn: Is my application file complete? — Your signature is missing from this page. — Do I sign here? And what is the deadline?
successCriteria: Transfer a contact detail accurately in the basic round.
Identify the missing item and confirm the stated deadline or route in the revisit.

revision.transferTaskEn: Ask a post-office partner which stamp a fictional letter needs.

gaps: Introduce identity/contact details earlier through a bridge without duplicate address IDs.
Distinguish submission and acknowledgement from approval.
Banking/payment support remains a scoped future gap; this is not a complete administration or immigration guide.

future.B1: Explain an application problem and follow up a delay.
future.B2: Understand and challenge complex service explanations with support.

topics.title: Finding a job

foundationA1.outcome: State a job goal and a full-time or part-time preference.

a2.outcome: In a short supported predictable exchange, ask how to apply, give one skill or past-work example and state availability.

communicativeTask.situation: A fictional vacancy and candidate profile
communicativeTask.promptEn: Recruiter has a vacancy with schedule and one skill requirement; candidate has a fictional profile. Use visible prompts to ask how to apply, give one relevant skill and agree a time. This is not a full spontaneous interview.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je voudrais postuler à ce poste. Je sais utiliser une caisse. — Quelles sont vos disponibilités ? — Je peux travailler le matin.
communicativeTask.modelEn: I would like to apply for this position. I know how to use a till. — When are you available? — I can work in the mornings.
successCriteria: State a job and schedule preference in the basic round.
Match one skill to the vacancy and exchange a concrete available time with support.

revision.transferTaskEn: Write a short fictional email asking which application documents are needed.

gaps: Introduce j’ai travaillé as a supported chunk before the later full Past bank; do not add a later-bank prerequisite.
Une expérience target and de l’expérience example require count/mass explanation, not silent ID merging.
A full spontaneous job interview is a future B1 demand; qualifications do not establish recognition or hiring success.

future.B1: Give a connected career account and handle follow-up interview questions.
future.B2: Argue for a professional proposal and negotiate complex role expectations.

topics.title: Talking about recent experiences

foundationA1.outcome: Proposed bridge, no current foundation/A1 lesson: recognise yesterday plus one fixed past-event chunk.

a2.outcome: Give a short past account in sequence and explain the outcome of a small incident.

communicativeTask.situation: Two people reconstruct a day from different cards
communicativeTask.promptEn: A sees places and activities; B sees times and a lost-key outcome. Ask what happened and reconstruct a short ordered account with a resolution.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Samedi, j’ai perdu mes clés. — Tu les as retrouvées ? — Oui, heureusement ! Elles étaient dans mon sac.
communicativeTask.modelEn: On Saturday, I lost my keys. — Did you find them? — Yes, fortunately! They were in my bag.
successCriteria: State a time and two linked past events, with visible support if needed.
Explain how the incident ended rather than list isolated verbs.

revision.transferTaskEn: Tell a two-event account about a missed bus with the same time and sequence tools.

gaps: Bound passé composé production and support c’était as evaluation before wider narrative-tense mastery.
Retrouvées agreement is explained for recognition, not an unsupported beginner production requirement.
Professional and lived expérience retain contextual IDs.

future.B1: Tell a connected story with background, causes and reactions.
future.B2: Shape a detailed narrative with perspective and nuanced temporal relationships.

topics.title: Preferences and simple comparisons

foundationA1.outcome: Proposed bridge, no current foundation/A1 lesson: recycle aimer and a fixed je préfère response from Leisure.

a2.outcome: Compare two familiar options and give a short practical reason for a choice.

communicativeTask.situation: Two offers with different constraints
communicativeTask.promptEn: A sees prices; B sees travel times or room qualities. Exchange information, choose together and give one comparison and a reason.
communicativeTask.modelFr: Je préfère cette chambre. Elle est plus calme que l’autre. — Mais elle est plus chère. — Oui, mais le calme est important pour moi.
communicativeTask.modelEn: I prefer this room. It is quieter than the other one. — But it is more expensive. — Yes, but peace and quiet matters to me.
successCriteria: Use information from both partners in the decision.
Make one accurate comparison and give a relevant reason; extended argument is not required.

revision.transferTaskEn: Compare cafés or transport options with a new constraint and the same reason frame.

gaps: Teach supported preference formulas earlier through Leisure while retaining this A2 comparison route.
Distinguish meilleur adjective from mieux adverb rather than merge their English glosses.
Sustained argument and formal debate remain future work.

future.B1: Support opinions with linked reasons and respond to a different view.
future.B2: Develop nuanced arguments, qualify comparisons and weigh counterarguments.
